# Training Log Running

## Summary
I settled into three runs a week this year and stuck to it, which is the first time the habit has held through a whole twelve months. The pattern was a short fast one on Tuesday, an easy one on Thursday and the long run on Sunday, with the rest days doing as much good as the running. The season's best came in October, a 5 km in 24:10 on the flat park course, which is a shade faster than I managed last year and felt controlled rather than desperate. The Sunday long run built steadily from eight kilometres in the spring to 14 km by the autumn, adding a kilometre every few weeks and backing off when the legs complained. I did not race anything longer than the 5 km and did not want to. The whole year was about consistency rather than heroics, and the numbers show it. I tracked every run in the same log, the distance, the rough pace and a word on how it felt, which is what let me see the shape of the season rather than guess at it. The easy runs were genuinely easy, slower than my pride wanted them to be, and that is what let the hard days actually be hard. I ran in the dark through the winter and in the early morning through the summer, and the timing mattered far less than turning up.

## Log
January was mostly easy running while I rebuilt after the winter break, three runs a week at a comfortable pace. February added a few strides and the legs came round. March brought an achilles niggle in the left leg, which I managed by dropping the fast Tuesday for two weeks and running everything easy until it settled. April was back to full weeks and the long run reached ten kilometres. May was the strongest month, with the cadence sitting around 174 and the easy pace dropping without effort. June lost a week to a cold that lingered, and July lost another, so the mileage dipped. August recovered with steady weeks and the long run back on track. September was consistent and the 5 km sharpened up. October produced the 24:10 and the long run touched 14 km. November eased off with the shorter days and the dark evenings. December was mostly easy running and a few hills, keeping the habit alive into the new year. The strongest stretch was May through June, where the weekly mileage held steady for eight weeks without a break. The weakest was the fortnight around the June cold, when I barely ran at all, and rebuilding afterwards took longer than the cold itself. I started the year with the long run at eight kilometres and finished it at fourteen, adding a kilometre every few weeks and holding each one for a fortnight before the next. The fast Tuesday sessions were the first thing I dropped whenever life got busy and the first thing I brought back when it eased.

## Notes
The shoes were retired after 700 km, which I tracked in the log, and the swap made an immediate difference to how the legs felt the day after a run. The achilles niggle in March was the one scare of the year and it taught me to back off early rather than push through, which is why it never became anything worse. My favourite session is the hill repeats on the bridge steps, short and brutal and over before I can talk myself out of it, and they seem to help the flat speed more than anything else I do. Cadence sits around 174 on the easy runs and a touch higher on the fast ones. The colds cost me the rhythm twice and I have stopped pretending they can be run through. Next year I want the same three runs a week, a 5 km under 24 minutes, and the long run to reach 16 km without the achilles complaining. The one thing I would change is the strength work, which I kept putting off and which might have saved me the March niggle in the first place. I will keep the hill repeats, though, since nothing else has done as much for the flat speed.
